capacity_mw_basis: contracted electric service; TeraWulf investor presentation separately lists Muskie as 800 MW critical IT pipeline capacity
status_detail: Site acquired in May 2026; zoned for intended use with permitting underway; electric service and related infrastructure agreements with Kentucky Power provide up to 1 GW of contracted electric service, with initial service expected in Q4 2028 and phased development thereafter.
why_not_in_baseline: New 2026 Eastern Kentucky industrial-park acquisition; baseline contains TeraWulf Lake Mariner/CB-5 but not Muskie or EastPark.

contradictions.description: May 2026 acquisition release and DCD describe approximately 285 acres of owned/controlled land, while TeraWulf's August 2026 SEC-filed Q2 update describes approximately 308 acres in Grayson. Treat 308 acres as the latest company-filed figure and retain 285 acres as acquisition-date context.

Company materials use both up to 1 GW of contracted electric service/gross campus capacity and 800 MW of critical IT pipeline capacity. data.json capacity_mw remains 1000 because the existing field tracks gross/contracted electric service, not critical IT load.

Regional public-media reporting on August 10, 2026 says TeraWulf's CEO discussed potentially doubling Muskie from 1 GW to 2 GW, but current TeraWulf filings reviewed for this refresh still evidence only up to 1 GW contracted electric service; do not promote to capacity_mw without a primary filing or utility record.

history.status: site acquired; zoned with permitting underway
history.note: Original discovery record before August 2026 refresh.
